subject: Zenith Health — Private Endpoint outbound controls & evidence
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@zenithhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Leah Kim <leah.kim@zenithhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint egress — quick checklist and evidence request

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The security team has a few final controls we need to validate before we sign the PO:

- A canonical list of IPs (or IP ranges) that Redwood's control plane and private endpoint runtime may originate outbound connections from. We need these for our firewall egress allowlist.
- An example firewall policy (short, vendor-agnostic) showing how to restrict egress to Redwood services and how to fail closed if the allowlist is not reachable.
- Any evidence or audit artifacts you can provide that prove the private endpoint respects source NATing semantics and does not leak customer private IPs to external destinations.

Can you send a single response with these items (or point me to a single bundle)? Leah (cc) is our security lead and will own the acceptance checklist. We are targeting a 24–48h turnaround.

Regards,
Sanjay
Director, Infrastructure Security
Zenith Health

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@zenithhealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Leah Kim <leah.kim@zenithhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — quick checklist and evidence request

Hi Sanjay / Leah,

Thanks — we can get you everything in one bundle. Short answers up front, then attachments/links below:

1) IPs for allowlisting: we provide stable customer-facing egress ranges for the control plane and a separate set of ephemeral runtime exit IPs (can be pinned via Dedicated). See attached CSV (redwood_private_ip_matrix.csv) for the canonical list and a column that indicates which ranges are "control-plane" vs "runtime-egress".

2) Firewall policy example: we include a vendor-agnostic policy snippet (in the PDF) showing least-privilege rules and a fail-closed default route.

3) Evidence/artifacts: we can share a short MOP (maintenance/operations playbook) that documents SNAT behavior and an audit sample showing outbound connections and NAT translation (we've redacted customer content).

Attachments: redwood_private_ip_matrix.csv; zenith_mop_checklist.pdf; screenshot-egress-rule-example.png

Next steps:
- Neha will attach a short write-up describing how the private connector performs source NAT and how logs are surfaced to customers.
- Aditya can follow up on options for pinning runtime egress to fixed IPs if you want that for tighter allowlisting.

I'll compile the bundle and upload to the Drive link in my next reply.

Best,
Kimberly Park
VP, Sales (Private Deployments)
Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@zenithhealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Leah Kim <leah.kim@zenithhealth.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — quick checklist and evidence request

Hi Sanjay / Leah,

Quick technical addendum here (pulling from our Private deployment runbook):

- SNAT model: the Redwood private connector performs SNAT at the runtime boundary. Customer-originating traffic never traverses our public-facing control plane unmodified; we translate source addresses to the configured egress IP/ips before forwarding to external services.

- Audit logs: when enabled, customers receive an "egress.audit" stream in the Console that includes: timestamp, source_connector_id, translated_source_ip, destination_ip, destination_port, tls_sni (when available), and token_id (hashed). We can provide a 48-hour sample (redacted) on request.

- Fail-closed guidance: configure a default deny for outbound + explicit allow rules for the pinned ranges. Example Firewall priority order: 1) Allow outbound to pinned Redwood control-plane ranges on ports 443 and 853 (dns) 2) Allow outbound to runtime pinned egress IPs on 443 3) Deny all other outbound.

I'll drop the 48h sample to the Drive link and also paste a short vendor-agnostic rule snippet below.

-- vendor-agnostic snippet --
# Example: minimal outbound allowlist
- policy: outbound-allowlist
  description: "Only allow traffic to Redwood control-plane and runtime egress ranges"
  rules:
    - allow: { dest_ranges: ["54.33.0.0/19", "3.5.120.0/22"] , ports: [443] }
    - allow: { dest_ranges: ["34.120.200.128/32"] , ports: [443] }
    - deny: { dest_ranges: ["0.0.0.0/0"] , ports: ["*"] }

If you want, Aditya and I can do a short walkthrough with your network team tomorrow morning to map this to your Palo Alto rules.

Thanks,
Neha
Senior Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@zenithhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Leah Kim <leah.kim@zenithhealth.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — quick checklist and evidence request

Kim / Neha,

This is helpful — thanks. A couple clarifying Qs after reviewing the snippet and the CSV:
1) Some of your runtime egress ranges look ephemeral in our early test environment. Do you have an SLA/contractual guarantee for pinned egress IPs if we take Dedicated or a pinned-edge option? We need a contractual statement for our firewall change window.
2) For the audit sample you mentioned: can you provide the 48-hour redacted sample with column headers and a small readme describing how fields map to our logs? Leah also asked if the Console export contains the original source private IP (we need to ensure it is never present in exported logs).

If we can get answers to those two items, we can sign off on the allowlist change this week.

—Sanjay

From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@zenithhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Leah Kim <leah.kim@zenithhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress — quick checklist and evidence request

Hi Sanjay / Leah,

Answers below:

1) Pinned IPs & contractual guarantees: yes — for Dedicated customers we offer a pinned egress option documented in the contract addendum. It guarantees a set of static egress IPs for the runtime pool for the duration of the contract term (we include change windows and rotation policies). I attached a short note in the Drive bundle and included the exact clause id in DocuSign (ZX-2777). If you want the IPs assigned to a single CIDR we can discuss allocation models (single /28 vs multiple /32s).

2) Audit sample and PII: the Console export never contains the original customer private source IP. We only surface the translated_source_ip in exports and logs. The 48-hour CSV we uploaded includes these headers: timestamp, source_connector_id, translated_source_ip, destination_ip, destination_port, tls_sni, token_id_hash. I pasted a 3-line sample below (redacted):

2026-09-10T02:14:03Z, conn-22a1, 34.120.200.128, 52.86.19.7, 443, api.partner.example.com, e3f9c1a2
2026-09-10T02:17:10Z, conn-22a1, 34.120.200.128, 3.5.120.11, 443, login.example.com, b7c6d4f2
2026-09-10T03:01:44Z, conn-22a1, 34.120.200.128, 52.86.19.7, 443, api.partner.example.com, c2a7e9b8

I also attached the redacted 48-hour CSV to the Drive link.

If that satisfies Leah's checklist, Kimberly — can we proceed to exchange the addendum and schedule the firewall change window?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Systems Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
